newsitem.title: USA: Washington Mutual, Great Western deal done.
newsitem.headline: Washington Mutual, Great Western deal done.

text.p: Washington Mutual Inc said Wednesday it completed its merger with Great Western Financial Corp, creating the nation's largest savings institution and the 11th-largest banking company in the United States based on year-end assets.

Under terms of the merger, Great Western shareholders will receive 0.9 share of Washington Mutual common stock for each share of Great Western common stock. Based on Tuesday's closing common stock price of $63.81, the share exchange is valued at approximately $8 billion, the company said.
The merger became effective last night.

As of March 31 the combined company would have had assets of $88.5 billion, deposits of $52.5 billion and served nearly four million households from more than 1,200 locations throughout the West and Florida.

Washington Mutual said it anticipates recording a net after-tax charge of approximately $318 million for transaction-related expenses, including a pre-tax addition of $100 million to Great Western's reserve for loan losses.

As part of the management transition, John Maher, Great Western's president and chief executive officer, and the other members of the Great Western Executive Management Committee will leave the company at the end of July.
Great Western said Maher declined to join the board of directors at this time, due to other commitments.
As part of the merger agreement, it said three Great Western outside board members will be joining the Washington Mutual board of directors immediately.
